statements.label: supported
statements.text: Circular RNAs are enriched within the MLL recombinome and can bind DNA to form circRNA:DNA hybrids at their matching loci.
statements.evidence: enriched within the MLL recombinome and can bind DNA, forming circRNA:DNA hybrids (circR loops) at their cognate loci
statements.note: The abstract states circRNAs are enriched in the MLL recombinome and bind DNA to form circR loops at their cognate loci.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: These circR loops form more readily in leukemia cells than in healthy haematopoietic progenitors.
statements.evidence: These circR loops promote transcriptional pausing, proteasome inhibition, chromatin re-organization, and DNA breakage.
statements.note: The abstract describes what circR loops do but never compares their formation between leukemic and healthy cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A potent oncogene can arise through chromosomal translocations joining the MLL gene to one of 100 possible translocation partners.
statements.evidence: chromosomal translocations between the mixed lineage leukemia (MLL) gene and one of 100 translocation partners
statements.note: The abstract describes the oncogene forming by translocations between MLL and one of 100 partners.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Overexpressing circRNAs in mouse leukemia xenografts generated new chromosomal translocations resembling the MLL recombinome and sped up disease onset.
statements.evidence: de novo generation of clinically relevant chromosomal translocations mimicking the MLL recombinome, and hastening of disease onset
statements.note: The abstract reports circRNA overexpression in xenografts generated MLL-like translocations and hastened disease onset.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The crosslinking method uncovered thousands of previously unrecognized snoRNA-mRNA interactions in human cells and mouse brain tissue.
statements.evidence: yielding thousands of previously unrecognized snoRNA-mRNA interactions in human cells and mouse brain tissues
statements.note: The abstract reports the method detected thousands of previously unrecognized snoRNA-mRNA interactions in human cells and mouse brain.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The three-way mRNA-SNORA73-7SL RNA interactions enhanced target mRNAs' association with the signal recognition particle, aiding secretion of the encoded proteins.
statements.evidence: The mRNA-SNORA73-7SL RNA interactions enhance the association of the SNORA73-target mRNAs with SRP, thereby facilitating the secretion of encoded proteins.
statements.note: The abstract states these three-way interactions enhance target mRNA association with SRP, facilitating secretion.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SNORA73 binds mRNAs encoding secretory and membrane proteins and also associates with the 7SL RNA component of the signal recognition particle.
statements.evidence: targets mRNAs that encode secretory proteins and membrane proteins. SNORA73 also interacts with 7SL RNA, part of the signal recognition particle (SRP)
statements.note: The abstract reports SNORA73 targets secretory and membrane protein mRNAs and interacts with 7SL RNA of the SRP.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The non-canonical snoRNA interactions are more abundant than the canonical modification-guiding interactions.
statements.evidence: Many interactions occur outside of snoRNA-guided RNA modification sites, hinting at non-canonical functions beyond RNA modification.
statements.note: The abstract notes many interactions fall outside modification sites but never says whether non-canonical interactions outnumber canonical ones.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Telomerase-positive neuroblastomas rely on the same TERRA m6A mechanism to maintain their telomeres.
statements.evidence: Telomerase-negative tumors maintain telomere length by alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT), but the underlying mechanism behind ALT remains poorly understood.
statements.note: The abstract studies ALT (telomerase-negative) tumors and never addresses whether telomerase-positive neuroblastomas use TERRA m6A.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: RNA methylation at the N6 position of adenosine in TERRA, installed by METTL3, is essential for telomere maintenance in ALT+ cells.
statements.evidence: RNA modification at the N6 position of internal adenosine (m6A) in TERRA by the methyltransferase METTL3 is essential for telomere maintenance in ALT+ cells
statements.note: The abstract states METTL3-deposited m6A on TERRA is essential for telomere maintenance in ALT+ cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: m6A is abundant on R-loop-enriched TERRA, and m6A-mediated recruitment of hnRNPA2B1 to TERRA is critical for R-loop formation.
statements.evidence: m6A modification is abundant in R-loop enriched TERRA, and the m6A-mediated recruitment of hnRNPA2B1 to TERRA is critical for R-loop formation
statements.note: The abstract reports m6A is abundant on R-loop-enriched TERRA and its recruitment of hnRNPA2B1 is critical for R-loop formation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Treating ALT+ neuroblastoma cells with a METTL3 inhibitor impaired TERRA's telomere targeting and caused DNA damage to build up at telomeres.
statements.evidence: treatment of ALT+ NB cells with a METTL3 inhibitor resulted in compromised telomere targeting of TERRA and accumulation of DNA damage at telomeres
statements.note: The abstract reports a METTL3 inhibitor compromised TERRA telomere targeting and caused DNA damage accumulation at telomeres.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Decreased inclusion of a 24-nucleotide neuron-specific microexon in CPEB4 is linked to idiopathic autism spectrum disorder.
statements.evidence: decreased inclusion of a 24-nucleotide neuron-specific microexon in CPEB4, a RNA-binding protein that regulates translation through cytoplasmic changes in poly(A) tail length, is linked to idiopathic autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
statements.note: The abstract states decreased inclusion of this 24-nucleotide CPEB4 microexon is linked to idiopathic ASD.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Neuronal CPEB4 assembles into condensates that disperse following depolarization, coinciding with a shift from translational repression to activation.
statements.evidence: neuronal CPEB4 forms condensates that dissolve after depolarization, a transition associated with a switch from translational repression to activation
statements.note: The abstract reports neuronal CPEB4 condensates dissolve after depolarization as translation switches from repression to activation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Restoring normal microexon inclusion in patient-derived neurons reverses autism-associated behaviours in mice.
statements.evidence: We conclude that the microexon is required in neuronal CPEB4 to preserve the reversible regulation of CPEB4-mediated gene expression in response to neuronal stimulation.
statements.note: The abstract concludes the microexon preserves reversible CPEB4 regulation but never tests behavioural rescue in any animal model.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Heterotypic interactions between the microexon and a histidine-residue cluster block irreversible CPEB4 aggregation by competing with homotypic histidine-cluster interactions.
statements.evidence: Heterotypic interactions between the microexon and a cluster of histidine residues prevent the irreversible aggregation of CPEB4 by competing with homotypic interactions between histidine clusters.
statements.note: The abstract states these heterotypic microexon-histidine interactions prevent irreversible CPEB4 aggregation by competing with homotypic ones.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LPHN3 builds synapses through two converging routes: Gα s signalling and recruitment of phase-separated postsynaptic scaffold proteins.
statements.evidence: LPHN3 organizes synapses through a convergent dual-pathway mechanism: activation of Gα s signalling and recruitment of phase-separated postsynaptic protein scaffolds
statements.note: The abstract states LPHN3 organizes synapses by a dual pathway: Gα s signalling and recruitment of phase-separated scaffolds.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Using CRISPR to switch LPHN3 from Gα s - to Gα 12/13 -coupled impaired synaptic connectivity as severely as deleting Lphn3 altogether.
statements.evidence: shifts LPHN3 from a Gα s - to a Gα 12/13 -coupled mode impaired synaptic connectivity as severely as the overall deletion of Lphn3
statements.note: The abstract reports CRISPR-driven switching to the Gα 12/13 mode impaired connectivity as severely as full Lphn3 deletion.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Activity in neurons promotes production of the synaptogenic, Gα s -coupled splice variant of LPHN3.
statements.evidence: neuronal activity promotes alternative splicing of the synaptogenic Gα s -coupled variant of LPHN3
statements.note: The abstract states neuronal activity promotes splicing toward the synaptogenic Gα s -coupled LPHN3 variant.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mutations that bias Lphn3 splicing toward the Gα 12/13 mode occur in people with neurodevelopmental disorders.
statements.evidence: Latrophilin-3 (encoded by Adgrl3, also known as Lphn3)-a postsynaptic adhesion G-protein-coupled receptor-mediates synapse formation in the hippocampus
statements.note: The study works in mice and never examines Lphn3 splice variants in people with neurodevelopmental disorders.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The other m6A readers YTHDC1, YTHDC2, and YTHDF2 compensate for PRRC2A loss in knockout testes.
statements.evidence: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) and its reader proteins YTHDC1, YTHDC2, and YTHDF2 have been shown to exert essential functions during spermatogenesis.
statements.note: The abstract names these readers as important in spermatogenesis but never tests whether they compensate when PRRC2A is lost.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Germ-cell-specific knockout of Prrc2a caused XY asynapsis and impaired meiotic sex chromosome inactivation in late-prophase spermatocytes.
statements.evidence: Germ cell-specific knockout of Prrc2a causes XY asynapsis and impaired meiotic sex chromosome inactivation in late-prophase spermatocytes
statements.note: The abstract reports Prrc2a knockout caused XY asynapsis and impaired meiotic sex chromosome inactivation in late-prophase spermatocytes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: PRRC2A decreases the RNA abundance of its target transcripts or improves their translation efficiency.
statements.evidence: PRRC2A decreases the RNA abundance or improves the translation efficiency of targeting transcripts
statements.note: The abstract states PRRC2A either lowers target RNA abundance or improves their translation efficiency.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: PRRC2A-null spermatocytes entered metaphase slowly, misaligned their chromosomes, formed disorganized spindles at metaphase I, and arrested there.
statements.evidence: PRRC2A-null spermatocytes exhibit delayed metaphase entry, chromosome misalignment, and spindle disorganization at metaphase I and are finally arrested at this stage
statements.note: The abstract reports PRRC2A-null spermatocytes had delayed metaphase entry, misaligned chromosomes, disorganized spindles, and arrest at metaphase I.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: NEAT1 deletion mutants assembled paraspeckles that became incorporated into nuclear speckles.
statements.evidence: We identified NEAT1 deletion mutants that assemble paraspeckles that are incorporated into nuclear speckles.
statements.note: The abstract reports certain NEAT1 deletion mutants assemble paraspeckles that get incorporated into nuclear speckles.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The shell proteins that segregate paraspeckles perform the same role for other membraneless organelles such as stress granules.
statements.evidence: This study shows that the paraspeckle shell composition dictates the independence of MLOs in the nucleus, providing insights into the importance of the shell in defining features and functions of MLOs.
statements.note: The abstract generalises conceptually to MLOs but tests only paraspeckles versus nuclear speckles, not stress granules.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The paraspeckle proteins SFPQ, HNRNPF and BRG1 block this incorporation, helping keep paraspeckles segregated from nuclear speckles.
statements.evidence: Several paraspeckle proteins, including SFPQ, HNRNPF and BRG1, prevent this incorporation and thus contribute to the segregation of paraspeckles from nuclear speckles.
statements.note: The abstract states SFPQ, HNRNPF and BRG1 prevent incorporation and help segregate paraspeckles from nuclear speckles.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: U2-related spliceosomal proteins instead act to internalize paraspeckles into nuclear speckles.
statements.evidence: Conversely, U2-related spliceosomal proteins are involved in internalizing the paraspeckles into nuclear speckles.
statements.note: The abstract reports U2-related spliceosomal proteins internalize paraspeckles into nuclear speckles.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: YTHDF1 expression was negatively correlated with the interferon-γ gene signature in TCGA colorectal cancer.
statements.evidence: YTHDF1 expression negatively correlated with interferon-γ gene signature in TCGA-CRC
statements.note: The abstract reports YTHDF1 expression negatively correlated with the interferon-γ signature in TCGA colorectal cancer.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: YTHDF1's clinical relevance was assessed in tissue microarray cohorts totalling 408 cases and a 526-sample TCGA cohort.
statements.evidence: Clinical significance of YTHDF1 was assessed in tissue microarrays (N=408) and TCGA (N=526) cohorts.
statements.note: The abstract states clinical significance was assessed in a 408-case tissue microarray set and a 526-sample TCGA cohort.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Single-cell RNA-seq of Ythdf1-knockout tumours revealed a drop in myeloid-derived suppressor cells together with a rise in cytotoxic T cells.
statements.evidence: scRNA-seq identified reduction of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), concomitant with increased cytotoxic T cells in Ythdf1 knockout tumours
statements.note: The abstract reports knockout tumours had fewer MDSCs and more cytotoxic T cells by single-cell RNA-seq.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: YTHDF1 inhibition sensitizes non-colorectal tumours such as melanoma to anti-PD1 therapy.
statements.evidence: targeting YTHDF1 by CRISPR (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats) or VNPs-si YTHDF1 boosted anti-PD1 efficacy in MSI-H CRC, and overcame anti-PD1 resistance in MSS CRC.
statements.note: The abstract shows YTHDF1 targeting improves anti-PD1 response in colorectal cancer but never tests other tumour types like melanoma.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Snhg9 also controls lipid absorption in the liver in addition to the small intestine.
statements.evidence: The intestinal microbiota regulates mammalian lipid absorption, metabolism, and storage.
statements.note: The abstract links Snhg9 to lipid handling in small intestinal epithelial cells and never examines the liver.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In mice, the gut microbiota reprogrammed intestinal lipid metabolism by silencing the lncRNA Snhg9 in small intestinal epithelial cells.
statements.evidence: the microbiota reprograms intestinal lipid metabolism in mice by repressing the expression of long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) Snhg9 (small nucleolar RNA host gene 9) in small intestinal epithelial cells
statements.note: The abstract reports the microbiota reprograms intestinal lipid metabolism by repressing Snhg9 in small intestinal epithelial cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Snhg9 lowered PPARγ activity by pulling the PPARγ inhibitor sirtuin 1 away from CCAR2.
statements.evidence: Snhg9 suppressed the activity of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ)-a central regulator of lipid metabolism-by dissociating the PPARγ inhibitor sirtuin 1 from cell cycle and apoptosis protein 2 (CCAR2).
statements.note: The abstract states Snhg9 suppressed PPARγ activity by dissociating its inhibitor sirtuin 1 from CCAR2.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Forcing Snhg9 expression in the intestinal epithelium of conventional mice impaired lipid absorption, reduced body fat, and protected mice from diet-induced obesity.
statements.evidence: Forced expression of Snhg9 in the intestinal epithelium of conventional mice impaired lipid absorption, reduced body fat, and protected against diet-induced obesity.
statements.note: The abstract reports forced Snhg9 expression impaired lipid absorption, reduced body fat, and protected against diet-induced obesity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Khib proteomic profiling across 20 matched primary and metastatic esophageal tumour samples, combined with CRISPR/Cas9 screening, identified NAT10 as a Khib substrate.
statements.evidence: systemic Khib proteome profiling in 20 paired primary esophageal tumor and metastatic tumor tissues with CRISPR/Cas9 functional screening, we identified N-acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10) as a substrate for Khib modification
statements.note: The abstract reports Khib profiling in 20 paired esophageal tumour samples plus CRISPR/Cas9 screening identified NAT10 as a Khib substrate.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The lysine modification Khib (2-hydroxyisobutyrylation) was markedly upregulated in cancer metastases, which is why the study focused on it.
statements.evidence: focused on 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation (Khib) due to its significant upregulation in cancer metastases
statements.note: The abstract states the study focused on Khib because it was significantly upregulated in cancer metastases.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The NAT10 inhibitor #7586-3507 showed no toxicity to normal esophageal tissue in the animal models.
statements.evidence: we discovered a lead compound #7586-3507 that inhibited NAT10 Khib modification and showed efficacy in tumor models in vivo at a low concentration
statements.note: The abstract reports the compound's in vivo efficacy at low dose but says nothing about its toxicity to normal tissue.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: NAT10 drives metastasis by raising NOTCH3 mRNA stability through N4-acetylcytidine modification.
statements.evidence: NAT10 in turn promotes metastasis by increasing NOTCH3 mRNA stability in an N4-acetylcytidine-dependent manner
statements.note: The abstract reports NAT10 promotes metastasis by increasing NOTCH3 mRNA stability in an N4-acetylcytidine-dependent manner.
